variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: missense, NP_000220.1:p.(Tyr135Asn). The papers describe the disease as autosomal recessive and caused by loss of LCAT function; the review also notes an intermediate (co-dominant) biochemical phenotype in heterozygous carriers.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.

carriers of one mutant LCAT allele show an intermediate biochemical phenotype between homozygous carriers and controls, suggesting that the disease, which is reported as recessive, is indeed co-dominant for the biochemical phenotype.

concerns: The variant appears only in a systematic review table (34256778) without a case description; the review does not name the original publication in the row, so the person-level data are second-hand.
Zygosity, phase and family data are not given in the review; the batch row records zygosity as not reported.
c.402G>T is listed in the same person at the adjacent nucleotide; the two may be one complex allele (cis) rather than two variants. Phase not reported.
The eGFR, anemia and proteinuria cells for this row are blank rather than 'Unk'.
notes_for_panel: One unclassified Dutch male (author Holleboom) listed with c.402G>T and c.403T>A. These are adjacent nucleotides (codons 134 and 135 by the batch's predicted protein). Phase is not reported: if both are on one allele they would be one complex change (c.402_403delinsTA) rather than two separate variants, and the person could be a single-allele carrier. Tabulated LCAT activity 71 nmol/mL/h. Candidates G-lcat-018 and G-lcat-019 come from the same table cell and should be adjudicated together.
